summary: Round 4's story notes are almost all closed, and the ending now says what it means. ch15-s09 pins a verdict slip, 'LEARNING + ACCOMPLICES / NEVER ONE PERSON', under WHO TAUGHT IT? (+12.08). The STATUS: OPEN stamp then strikes the CASE FILE, not the question, so the film no longer seems to take back its own answer. The three-stamp motif can now be heard: fx-stamp-fence 1906.87, fx-stamp-howfar 2103.89 and fx-stamp 2122.00, rising -32/-31/-29. Its middle beat can be seen too: ch15-s08 pushes onto HOW FAR? HOW FAST? and stamps it in large red at +37.92. ch15-s08 also opens on a fast-forward (knob, snow, fans, Go board, +0.96 to +3.96) that mirrors the ch01-s06 rewind, a quiet bookend. ch15-s06 is finally clean: no hand, no Hassabis caption, and the flame blooms on the stage candle. L1502 now carries the Versailles callback, so Hopfield's 'nobody remembered' is paid off 25 minutes later. ch15-s05's opening wide names all four labs. Four things keep story at 8.5. (1) ch15-s03 is the film's only look inside the 'dark lantern', and its visual shows the decisive experiment (snuff 'rabbit', get 'habit') that the narration never says. A first-time viewer sees a word swap explained only by a mono caption. (2) The film's final stamp (ch15-s09) is now the faintest of the three, struck half off the folder edge, although it is the loudest in sound. (3) The Nobel call, the crest of Hinton's 36-year arc, plays to an empty bedroom: no Hinton, and the phone lights about 0.7 s after 'rings'. (4) L0114 is better (221 to 194 wpm) but is still among the fastest lines in the film. The film runs 36.1 min (113% of target), and the ch14 to ch15-s05 present-day run (about 4.5 min) is still dense. It now flows into a moving close (s06-s10), so I accept it.

issues.problem: ch15-s03 is the film's one look inside the 'dark lantern' that ch15-s08 later declares still dark. The sheet shows the experiment that proves planning: a snuffer drops on the RABBIT lantern at b3 (11.54), a neighbour lights, and the line resolves to HABIT, captioned 'rabbit → (suppressed) → habit'. The narration says only 'it chose rabbit before writing the line. Nobody told it to plan.' So the decisive step (take the plan away and the model re-plans) is told only by a mono caption, and a first-time viewer sees a word change for no stated reason during the punchline. The claim is in the bible (claims.json: 'suppressing it yields habit').

best_moments: ch01-s01 / ch15-s09: the film opens on a lone cyan cursor and closes by returning to one. A neighbour's lamp comes on, and a match is struck on 'candles'. A true bookend.
ch01-s06 / ch15-s08: a rewind montage (Go stone, fans, snow, knob, lantern) carries us back to 1943. Thirty-four minutes later the same images run forward as the case board rewires into a network.
ch02-s04 / L0209: 'Each belief gets one, burning as long as it was held.' One rule turns 80 years into a bar chart in wax, and it pays off in ch15-s08's 'some, two; one match, a day'.
ch04-s05: 'In 1971, on his forty-third birthday, Frank Rosenblatt drowned while sailing.' Then the handwritten dedication in the second printing of Perceptrons. Still the film's best quiet beat.
ch05-s01 / ch15-s01: Hopfield's Versailles talk that 'nobody remembered hearing' is paid off at the Nobel, in a hall of mirrors.
ch06-s05 to ch07-s01: 'So who paid for dinner? Keep that question.' ... 'Both men. Each man lost one bet.'
ch08-s12 / L0823: the error drops 10.9 points and the narrator says only 'A cliff.'
ch08-s13b: 'Why choose the fog?' The learned tiles snap out of the fog, and Hinton, at the edge of the light for thirty-six years, is at the desk when the pool reaches him: 'Now, it found him.'
ch12-s06: 'Not a new engine. A new door.' One warm window in a city of cold ones.
ch14-s02 to ch14-s07: 'CAN A FENCE AROUND CHIPS HOLD?' comes back stamped STATUS: OPEN on 'stands', now with its own soft clack. The first beat of a three-stamp rule the ear learns.
ch15-s07: Widrow's lantern in a snowy window, 'never got over it'. 'Remember him' is paid off 32 minutes after it was planted.

ch15-s08 to ch15-s09: 'Never one person. The board was a network all along.' HOW FAR? HOW FAST? is stamped open, and the verdict slip LEARNING + ACCOMPLICES / NEVER ONE PERSON closes one question while the case file itself stays open.
